messages:
liam: quick sync — loadlab run 2026-03-15 showing ~18% p99 tail regression on H100 vs A100 for kv-heavy replay. full csv in drive, but numbers look consistent across 3 runs :confused:

sasha: ugh. which driver / cuda / image were those H100 runs on?

bench-bot: summary: gpu=H100 driver=535.86 cuda=12.1 image=ghcr.io/redwood/runtime:cuda12.1-rt-20260314 kernel_flags="nvidia_drm.modeset=1 nvidia_uvm.enable=1" run_id=run-2145 p99=190ms p50=22ms qps=120
bench-bot: baseline A100 driver=525.85 cuda=11.8 image=ghcr.io/redwood/runtime:cuda11.8-rt-20260309 p99=160ms p50=20ms qps=125

omar: interesting — same model and batch config?

liam: yeah identical model binary, same seq len distribution (median 64, tail 512), batching heuristics set to `dynamic_small_first` in loadgen.

sasha: any difference in kernel_selector output? recall H100 sometimes picks different matmul kernels for small heads.

jess: i grabbed a profiler trace. high-level: KV cache miss/evict spikes on H100 around heavy multi-client mixes, and kernel-selection shows repeated churn between small-tile and large-tile GEMM kernels.

liam: here's the minimal repro command I used (copy/paste):
```
./loadgen --mode=replay --trace=kv-heavy.trace --clients=40 --batching=dynamic_small_first \
  --model=/mnt/models/llm-xx/compiled.bin --image=ghcr.io/redwood/runtime:cuda12.1-rt-20260314
```

omar: try forcing kernel_selector override? in runtime config: `kernel_selector=prefer_large` — on my last run that stops the churn.

jess: confirmed locally — forcing `prefer_large` on H100 dropped p99 from 190ms -> 170ms and reduced kernel churn in the trace. not full parity but closer.

sasha: that smells like a selector threshold problem tuned for A100 tile shapes. could be CUDA library version behavior too.

katie: proposed matrix for controlled experiment (will add to loadlab job):
- GPUs: [A100, H100]
- Drivers: [525.85.12, 535.86.05]
- CUDA: [11.8, 12.1]
- Images: [ghcr.io/redwood/runtime:cuda11.8-rt-20260309, ghcr.io/redwood/runtime:cuda12.1-rt-20260314]
- Kernel flags: ["nvidia_uvm.enable=0", "nvidia_uvm.enable=1"]
- Kernel selector: [auto, prefer_large]

omar: i'll run the matrix overnight and collect:
- nvprof/Nsight sampling on first 30s
- perf counters for SM occupancy and L2 utilization
- kernel selection logs (runtime --debug=kselector)

liam: please also capture `nvidia-smi -q` and `cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version` and `uname -a` for each run.

bench-bot: added job job-2145-matrix to queue. estimated runtime ~14h given permutations.

jess: one more thing — KV cache policy: we're recomputing too aggressively for some client mixes. can we try enabling `kvcache.prefetch=on` in the harness for a subset of runs?

sasha: yes, add `kvcache.prefetch=on/off` to the matrix. hypothesize prefetch will reduce evictions and smooth kernel load.

katie: i'll open a small PR to the loadlab harness with the matrix + artifact upload (perf, nvprof, kernel-logs). tagging @devex for image tagging notes.

liam: priority list for tomorrow:
1) run matrix and gather artifacts (omar)
2) compare kernel_selector traces and perf counters (jess + sasha)
3) try kvcache.prefetch toggle (bench)
4) if driver difference shows up, escalate to infra/eng-sre for driver pin/coord (liam)

omar: on it. will drop a short summary thread when runs finish :eyes:

katie: thanks team :thumbsup:
